newsitem.title: USA: 10 children reported found in N.J. crack house.
newsitem.headline: 10 children reported found in N.J. crack house.

text.p: Ten children were found abandoned in a crack house where they had been living for weeks on canned vegetables with no heat, water or electricity, area media reported Friday.
The children, ranging in age from about one to 16, were found after a caller alerted authorities of a strong smell of kerosene on the property, Philadelphia radio station KYW reported.
Three of the children were being examined at a local hospital.

According to the reports, some of the children said they came from Philadelphia and Trenton, New Jersey, and there was considerable evidence of drug activity in the house. The children had been in the house for about three weeks.
Atlantic City police referred calls to the New Jersey Division of Youth and Family Services, saying the police had participated in the case but the agency had jurisdiction.

A spokeswoman for the agency said she could not comment on the report. In general, she said, the department would treat instances of abandoned children by first trying to find their parents or close relatives.
If that failed, the children would be placed in foster care and could be put in adoptive homes if they were ruled to have been permanently abandoned.
